title: Status of the World's Soil Resources: Main Report
organization: FAO & Intergovernmental Technical Panel on Soils (ITPS)
abstract: Global assessment of soil condition and threats, including soil organic carbon decline, compiled by FAO and the Intergovernmental Technical Panel on Soils.
limitations: Global synthesis report; regional/local conditions can differ substantially from global averages.
license_notes: FAO open-access report; summary metadata only used here, full text not redistributed.

title: Large-scale drivers of relationships between soil microbial properties and organic carbon across Europe
abstract: Continental-scale observational study examining how soil microbial properties (including microbial respiration) relate to soil organic carbon across European soils.
limitations: Correlational, large-scale observational data across Europe; relationship strength varies with climate and land management and was not established for semi-arid or tropical systems.

title: Landscape perspectives on agricultural intensification and biodiversity – ecosystem service management
abstract: Highly-cited review of how agricultural intensification and landscape-scale habitat heterogeneity affect biodiversity and ecosystem services such as pollination and biological pest control.
limitations: A synthesis/review; specific effect sizes vary by region, taxon, and landscape context.

title: Effects of Habitat Fragmentation on Biodiversity
organization: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
abstract: Classic review distinguishing effects of habitat amount from effects of fragmentation per se on biodiversity, concluding fragmentation-per-se effects are frequently weaker and more context-dependent than commonly assumed.
limitations: Review synthesis; the author explicitly notes fragmentation-per-se effects are often smaller than habitat-amount effects and are not uniformly negative.

title: European agroforestry has no unequivocal effect on biodiversity: a time-cumulative meta-analysis
abstract: Time-cumulative meta-analysis of European agroforestry studies finding that overall effects on biodiversity are inconsistent and not unequivocally positive, though some subsystems (e.g. silvoarable) showed gains relative to cropland in parts of the dataset.
limitations: Findings are specific to European agroforestry systems; explicitly concludes there is no unequivocal overall biodiversity benefit — outcomes are system- and context-dependent.

title: Research on agroforestry systems and biodiversity conservation: what can we conclude so far and what should we improve?
abstract: Synthesis of agroforestry-biodiversity research concluding that evidence is heterogeneous across studies and calling for standardized methodology to enable robust comparison.
limitations: Meta-synthesis identifies methodological heterogeneity across the underlying literature; treat effect direction/magnitude as context-dependent, not a fixed quantitative estimate.

title: Pesticides and Soil Invertebrates: A Hazard Assessment
abstract: Hazard assessment reviewing evidence that pesticide exposure poses risks to non-target soil and arthropod invertebrates.
limitations: DOI inferred from Frontiers' standard DOI-URL naming convention, not independently confirmed via a CrossRef lookup. Hazard assessment synthesis; site-specific impact depends on pesticide type, dose, timing, and species sensitivity.

title: Climate change and the global redistribution of biodiversity: substantial variation in empirical support for expected range shifts
abstract: Systematic review evaluating empirical support for climate-driven species range shifts, finding substantial variation in outcomes across taxa and regions rather than a uniform pattern.
limitations: The review explicitly reports substantial variation in empirical support; range-shift direction and magnitude are not uniformly predictable from temperature/rainfall change alone.

title: Effects of Long-Term Vegetation Restoration on Distribution of Deep Soil Moisture in Semi-arid Northwest of China
authors: Journal of Soil Science and Plant Nutrition authors
organization: Journal of Soil Science and Plant Nutrition (Springer)
abstract: Long-term field study on the Loess Plateau (semi-arid northwest China) examining how vegetation restoration type affects deep soil moisture distribution.
limitations: Findings are specific to semi-arid northwest China restoration plots with particular soil and vegetation types; transferability to other semi-arid regions requires local validation.

title: Combined impacts of deforestation and wildlife trade on tropical biodiversity are severely underestimated
abstract: Analysis finding that 89% of assessed species experienced average habitat losses of 16% from deforestation, and that combined pressure with wildlife trade raised average losses for exploited species to approximately 54%.
limitations: Findings focus on tropical forest ecosystems and species also exposed to wildlife trade; not directly generalizable to non-tropical ecosystems or non-traded taxa.

title: A review of indicators and methods to assess biodiversity
abstract: FAO review surveying indicators and methods (including species richness) used to assess biodiversity in agricultural and natural systems.
limitations: Publication year was not confirmed via automated search; treat as a methodological reference rather than a primary quantitative source.

title: Intercropping enhances beneficial arthropods and controls pests: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Systematic review and meta-analysis (63 articles, 18 countries) finding intercropping increased beneficial arthropod abundance by 36%, density by 94%, and species richness by 27% relative to monoculture.
limitations: Publication year not confirmed via automated search (metadata partial pending manual verification). Meta-analytic averages; magnitude varies by crop combination, region, and taxa.
